persistedQueryReceipts.scope: The anonymous AVSpec search interface explicitly searches published observations. Only rows returned by that interface and anonymously downloadable from the matching official record identifier are eligible. AAVSO states that its hosted data may be used in publications when the current Data Usage Guidelines are followed.

AAVSO states that International Database observations are freely available to the community for research and publication subject to its current Data Usage Guidelines. The v2 JSON API requires token authentication for access; authentication is not treated as a grant of proprietary rights. Only exact target-name and bounded date results from the documented photometry endpoint are eligible.

Only public ADS bibliographic metadata is retained. CTAS does not download, mirror, or assert reuse rights for article full text; publisher and repository links retain their own access and reuse terms. Event association requires an exact retained transient name.

ASAS-SN describes Sky Patrol light curves as public and provides publication citations. CTAS may link an operator to the official HTTPS coordinate-query page. No automated provider-data request was sent. The official legacy HTTPS query form requires reCAPTCHA and says users needing more than 100 light curves should contact ASAS-SN. The published V2 client and documentation currently use an unencrypted HTTP API, while the linked HTTPS V2 host and client repository are unavailable. CTAS therefore withholds automatic ingestion until ASAS-SN publishes a current secure, bounded machine-access contract. This is an interface-integrity boundary, not a claim that the public light-curve data are proprietary.

Official registered public forced-photometry service. ATLAS requires Tonry et al. (2018), Smith et al. (2020) for transient time-domain science, Shingles et al. (2021) for the web service, and the current acknowledgment published on the official forced-photometry home page.

The adapter uses ESO's anonymous TAP service only and retains a reduced-product row only when obs_release_date is present and no later than the query time. ESO states that the proprietary period protects raw and derived data until release and distributes archive data under CC BY 4.0 with acknowledgment requirements. No product bytes are downloaded.

Gaia DR3 is a public ESA data release and ESA identifies CDS as an official Gaia partner data centre. This anonymous adapter is allowlisted to the VizieR copy of catalogue I/355/gaiadr3, stores catalog rows and provider links only, and does not query unrelated VizieR collections or retrieve DataLink products.
No partial, malformed, or public-state-ambiguous mission row was stored.

The adapter is anonymous and restricted to the provider-documented public AllWISE Source Catalog and 2MASS Point Source Catalog. It stores catalog rows and official links only; proprietary/exclusive-access IRSA holdings are outside the allowlist.
Only observation and product rows explicitly marked PUBLIC are retained. Product bytes remain provider-hosted; this system stores metadata and official download links only.
NED host queries require one unambiguous host identity; transient coordinates are not silently substituted.

The anonymous public NED TAP service documents programmatic cone searches of the NED Object Directory and requests NED acknowledgment. CTAS retains bounded source-native rows and provenance only. NED states that high-volume automated access is best-effort, so this adapter is single-threaded, starts at most one request per second, and never queries proprietary or user-account holdings.

NOIRLab's provider-owned API authentication notebook states that anyone may retrieve public files while proprietary-file retrieval requires authorization. This adapter sends no credential and retains a product only after an exact file-metadata lookup supplies a nonblank release_date no later than the query time. Anonymous metadata about unreleased files is counted only for exclusion and is never stored. Product bytes are not downloaded.

This is an interface-integrity boundary, not a claim that the public light-curve data are proprietary.

evidence_timeline.summary: We report on observations of the optical counterpart of GRB 261007A detected by SVOM/ECLAIRs and SVOM/GRM (Goto et al., GCN 45824), Einstein Probe WXT and FXT (EP261007a, Wen et al., GCN 45828), and Fermi GBM (Malacaria, GCN 45830). We observed the field of GRB 261007A / EP261007a with a Las Cumbres Observatory (LCO) 40-cm telescope located at the LCO node at McDonald Observatory, Texas, with 180-sec exposures in each of the SDSS ǵ, ŕ, and i' filters. The first observation started on 2026-10-07 at 07:07:24 UT, about 1.4225 hr after the SVOM trigger. The optical counterpart first detected with KAIT by Zheng et al. (GCN 45825) is clearly detected in all bands. We measure the following AB magnitudes, calibrated against PanSTARRS-1 DR2 stars and not corrected for Galactic extinction: Date (UT, mid-time) | filter | mag | error | mid t - t0 (hr) ----------------------------------------------------------------------- 2026-10-07T07:08:54 | g' | 18.59 | 0.06 | 1.4475 2026-10-07T07:12:04 | r' | 18.33 | 0.08 | 1.5003 2026-10-07T07:15:11 | i' | 18.10 | 0.16 | 1.5522 Our results are consistent with other optical and near-IR detections: Saccardi et al. (GCN 45829, spectroscopic redshift of 2.101), Mohan et al. (GCN 45832), Saccardi et al. (GCN 45837), Shi et al. (GCN 45838), An et al. (GCN 45840), Arya et al. (GCN 45841), Rehemtulla et al. (ZTF26abzxgsr, GCN 45843), and Fracile et al. (AT 2026aepi, TNS Astronomical Transient Report No. 327228). Based on observations made with the Las Cumbres Observatory's education network telescopes that were upgraded through generous support from the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation (LCO program IAC2026B-010). These observations are part of a course in Astrophysical Techniques of the Master in Astrophysics of the Astrophysics Department of the University of La Laguna in collaboration with the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (La Laguna, Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain).
evidence_timeline.title: GRB 261007A / EP261007a: ULL-ASTRO-MASTER detection of the optical afterglow with LCO 40-cm telescope at McDonald Observatory

evidence_timeline.summary: We report on ZTF and P60/SEDM follow-up of the optical counterpart (Zheng et al., GCN 45825; Saccardi et al., GCN 45829; Mohan et al., GCN 45832; Saccardi et al., GCN 45837, Shi et al., GCN 45838, Arya et al., GCN 45841) to GRB 261007A (Goto et al., GCN 45824). The counterpart was automatically discovered in ZTF data by the BTSbot machine learning model (Rehemtulla et al. 2024) at 2026-10-07 08:14, independent of the GRB trigger. BTSbot autonomously requested P60/SEDM follow-up, which was carried out 34 minutes later (2026-10-07 08:48). The SEDM spectrum is at ultra low-resolution (R~100) and shows only a continuum. ZTFReST (Andreoni et al. 2021) and other fast transient filters developed within the ZTF Collaboration also identified ZTF26abzxgsr as a candidate fast transient independent of the GRB trigger. The ZTF observations were conducted as part of the 1-day cadence public gri survey overlapping the Rubin-LSST Wide-Fast-Deep footprint. publication_revisions.abstract: We report on observations of the optical counterpart of GRB 261007A detected by SVOM/ECLAIRs and SVOM/GRM (Goto et al., GCN 45824), Einstein Probe WXT and FXT (EP261007a, Wen et al., GCN 45828), and Fermi GBM (Malacaria, GCN 45830). We observed the field of GRB 261007A / EP261007a with a Las Cumbres Observatory (LCO) 40-cm telescope located at the LCO node at McDonald Observatory, Texas, with 180-sec exposures in each of the SDSS ǵ, ŕ, and i' filters. The first observation started on 2026-10-07 at 07:07:24 UT, about 1.4225 hr after the SVOM trigger. The optical counterpart first detected with KAIT by Zheng et al. (GCN 45825) is clearly detected in all bands. We measure the following AB magnitudes, calibrated against PanSTARRS-1 DR2 stars and not corrected for Galactic extinction: Date (UT, mid-time) | filter | mag | error | mid t - t0 (hr) ----------------------------------------------------------------------- 2026-10-07T07:08:54 | g' | 18.59 | 0.06 | 1.4475 2026-10-07T07:12:04 | r' | 18.33 | 0.08 | 1.5003 2026-10-07T07:15:11 | i' | 18.10 | 0.16 | 1.5522 Our results are consistent with other optical and near-IR detections: Saccardi et al. (GCN 45829, spectroscopic redshift of 2.101), Mohan et al. (GCN 45832), Saccardi et al. (GCN 45837), Shi et al. (GCN 45838), An et al. (GCN 45840), Arya et al. (GCN 45841), Rehemtulla et al. (ZTF26abzxgsr, GCN 45843), and Fracile et al. (AT 2026aepi, TNS Astronomical Transient Report No. 327228). Based on observations made with the Las Cumbres Observatory's education network telescopes that were upgraded through generous support from the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation (LCO program IAC2026B-010). These observations are part of a course in Astrophysical Techniques of the Master in Astrophysics of the Astrophysics Department of the University of La Laguna in collaboration with the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (La Laguna, Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain).

publication_revisions.abstract: We report on ZTF and P60/SEDM follow-up of the optical counterpart (Zheng et al., GCN 45825; Saccardi et al., GCN 45829; Mohan et al., GCN 45832; Saccardi et al., GCN 45837, Shi et al., GCN 45838, Arya et al., GCN 45841) to GRB 261007A (Goto et al., GCN 45824). The counterpart was automatically discovered in ZTF data by the BTSbot machine learning model (Rehemtulla et al. 2024) at 2026-10-07 08:14, independent of the GRB trigger. BTSbot autonomously requested P60/SEDM follow-up, which was carried out 34 minutes later (2026-10-07 08:48). The SEDM spectrum is at ultra low-resolution (R~100) and shows only a continuum. ZTFReST (Andreoni et al. 2021) and other fast transient filters developed within the ZTF Collaboration also identified ZTF26abzxgsr as a candidate fast transient independent of the GRB trigger. The ZTF observations were conducted as part of the 1-day cadence public gri survey overlapping the Rubin-LSST Wide-Fast-Deep footprint. The source (ZTF26abzxgsr / AT 2026aepi) was detected in ZTF gri images and was not detected the previous night. | Obs time (UTC) | Time since SVOM detection (2026-10-07 05:42:03) (hh:mm:ss) | Band | Alert mag (AB) | Mag unc | |---------------------|----------|------|-------|---------| | 2026-10-06 06:02:24 | - | r | >19.96 | non-det | | 2026-10-06 08:35:41 | - | i | >19.75 | non-det | | 2026-10-06 09:23:14 | - | g | >19.92 | non-det | | 2026-10-07 06:02:02 | 00:19:59 | r | 17.16 | 0.032 | | 2026-10-07 06:34:56 | 00:52:53 | i | 17.83 | 0.067 | | 2026-10-07 07:33:02 | 01:50:59 | g | 18.84 | 0.088 | Magnitudes are not corrected for Galactic extinction. Based on observations obtained with the Samuel Oschin Telescope 48-inch and the 60-inch Telescope at the Palomar Observatory as part of the Zwicky Transient Facility project. publications.abstract: We report on observations of the optical counterpart of GRB 261007A detected by SVOM/ECLAIRs and SVOM/GRM (Goto et al., GCN 45824), Einstein Probe WXT and FXT (EP261007a, Wen et al., GCN 45828), and Fermi GBM (Malacaria, GCN 45830). We observed the field of GRB 261007A / EP261007a with a Las Cumbres Observatory (LCO) 40-cm telescope located at the LCO node at McDonald Observatory, Texas, with 180-sec exposures in each of the SDSS ǵ, ŕ, and i' filters. The first observation started on 2026-10-07 at 07:07:24 UT, about 1.4225 hr after the SVOM trigger. The optical counterpart first detected with KAIT by Zheng et al. (GCN 45825) is clearly detected in all bands. We measure the following AB magnitudes, calibrated against PanSTARRS-1 DR2 stars and not corrected for Galactic extinction: Date (UT, mid-time) | filter | mag | error | mid t - t0 (hr) ----------------------------------------------------------------------- 2026-10-07T07:08:54 | g' | 18.59 | 0.06 | 1.4475 2026-10-07T07:12:04 | r' | 18.33 | 0.08 | 1.5003 2026-10-07T07:15:11 | i' | 18.10 | 0.16 | 1.5522 Our results are consistent with other optical and near-IR detections: Saccardi et al. (GCN 45829, spectroscopic redshift of 2.101), Mohan et al. (GCN 45832), Saccardi et al. (GCN 45837), Shi et al. (GCN 45838), An et al. (GCN 45840), Arya et al. (GCN 45841), Rehemtulla et al. (ZTF26abzxgsr, GCN 45843), and Fracile et al. (AT 2026aepi, TNS Astronomical Transient Report No. 327228). Based on observations made with the Las Cumbres Observatory's education network telescopes that were upgraded through generous support from the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation (LCO program IAC2026B-010). These observations are part of a course in Astrophysical Techniques of the Master in Astrophysics of the Astrophysics Department of the University of La Laguna in collaboration with the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (La Laguna, Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain).

publications.abstract: We report on ZTF and P60/SEDM follow-up of the optical counterpart (Zheng et al., GCN 45825; Saccardi et al., GCN 45829; Mohan et al., GCN 45832; Saccardi et al., GCN 45837, Shi et al., GCN 45838, Arya et al., GCN 45841) to GRB 261007A (Goto et al., GCN 45824). The counterpart was automatically discovered in ZTF data by the BTSbot machine learning model (Rehemtulla et al. 2024) at 2026-10-07 08:14, independent of the GRB trigger. BTSbot autonomously requested P60/SEDM follow-up, which was carried out 34 minutes later (2026-10-07 08:48). The SEDM spectrum is at ultra low-resolution (R~100) and shows only a continuum. ZTFReST (Andreoni et al. 2021) and other fast transient filters developed within the ZTF Collaboration also identified ZTF26abzxgsr as a candidate fast transient independent of the GRB trigger. The ZTF observations were conducted as part of the 1-day cadence public gri survey overlapping the Rubin-LSST Wide-Fast-Deep footprint. The source (ZTF26abzxgsr / AT 2026aepi) was detected in ZTF gri images and was not detected the previous night. | Obs time (UTC) | Time since SVOM detection (2026-10-07 05:42:03) (hh:mm:ss) | Band | Alert mag (AB) | Mag unc | |---------------------|----------|------|-------|---------| | 2026-10-06 06:02:24 | - | r | >19.96 | non-det | | 2026-10-06 08:35:41 | - | i | >19.75 | non-det | | 2026-10-06 09:23:14 | - | g | >19.92 | non-det | | 2026-10-07 06:02:02 | 00:19:59 | r | 17.16 | 0.032 | | 2026-10-07 06:34:56 | 00:52:53 | i | 17.83 | 0.067 | | 2026-10-07 07:33:02 | 01:50:59 | g | 18.84 | 0.088 | Magnitudes are not corrected for Galactic extinction. All times are in UTC. BTSbot processes alerts in the BOOM alert broker (Jegou du Laz et al. 2026) and interfaces with follow-up facilities through the SkyPortal marshal (Coughlin et al. 2023). Based on observations obtained with the Samuel Oschin Telescope 48-inch and the 60-inch Telescope at the Palomar Observatory as part of the Zwicky Transient Facility project.
